result.text: Prophylaxis failure through Week 24 occurred in 38% of letermovir subjects vs 61% of placebo; clinically significant CMV infection by Week 24 in 18% vs 42%. Stratum-adjusted treatment difference -23.5 (95% CI -32.5, -14.6); p<0.0001.

target_moa.text: Letermovir is an inhibitor of the CMV DNA terminase complex (encoded by UL56/UL89), which is necessary for generation of unit-length viral DNA genomes; this is a novel mechanism of action distinct from DNA polymerase inhibitors.

citations.quote: Letermovir is an inhibitor of the cytomegalovirus (CMV) terminase complex. This is a novel mechanism of action and therefore cross-resistance with other currently available anti-CMV drugs is not anticipated.

citations.quote: Letemovir is a new molecular entity (NME). It is an antiviral agent with activity against human cytomegalovirus (CMV) with a novel mechanism of action, targeting the CMV terminase complex.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and ≥2% greater than placebo) were nausea (27% vs 23%), diarrhea (26% vs 24%), vomiting (19% vs 14%), peripheral edema (14% vs 9%), cough (14% vs 10%), headache (14% vs 9%), fatigue (13% vs 11%), and abdominal pain (12% vs 9%). Cardiac adverse event rate was higher with PREVYMIS (13%) vs placebo (6%).

On February 27, 2017, Breakthrough therapy designation was granted for IV and oral letemovir for the prevention of CMV infection and/or disease in adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of allogeneic HSCT.

The clinical efficacy and safety of letemovir is primarily supported by one phase 3 trial (P001) evaluating letemovir (tablets and intravenous solution) compared to placebo and one phase 2b dose-ranging trial (P020) that also included a placebo comparison.
